claims.text: The FOMC maintained its target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 0-1/4 percent (rate decision not explicitly shown in the provided excerpts; the excerpts only state the Committee's commitment to full policy support).

citations.quotation: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals.

claims.text: The Committee continues asset purchases of at least $80 billion per month of Treasury securities and at least $40 billion per month of agency mortgage-backed securities, continuing until substantial further progress toward its goals, with the pace/duration open-ended and progress assessed at coming meetings.

citations.quotation: it would continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage‑backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward its maximum employment and price stability goals. Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals, and the Committee will continue to assess progress in coming meetings.

claims.text: The Committee identified that the path of the economy depends on the virus and that risks to the economic outlook remain, and it stands ready to adjust policy if risks emerge that could impede attainment of its goals.

citations.quotation: The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain.

claims.text: The Committee would adjust monetary policy if risks emerge that impede its goals, monitoring public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and expectations, and financial/international developments.

citations.quotation: The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals.

counterarguments.text: Inflation risk was downplayed: the statement characterized rising inflation as largely transitory, so one could argue the Committee did not treat inflation as a principal risk despite it having risen.

citations.quotation: Inflation has risen, largely reflecting transitory factors.

counterarguments.text: Financial conditions were described as accommodative, suggesting the Committee did not identify tightening financial conditions as a current risk.

citations.quotation: Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.
